meta.title: Dawny: the iPhone to-do app that resets every night
meta.description: Dawny ends your day at 3 a.m.: what you finished is filed away, what you didn't moves to the archive. A to-do app for iPhone, free, and without an account.
meta.ogAlt: Dawny, a clean list every morning

hero.headline: A clean list every morning.
hero.lead: What you take on for today counts. At 3 a.m. everything resets: what you finished is filed away, what you didn't moves to the archive instead of piling up. In the morning you decide again what really matters today.
hero.ctaNote: Free. No subscription, no ads, no account.
hero.imageAlt: The Today view of Dawny on the iPhone with open and completed tasks

demo.heading: Three lists, one philosophy.
demo.line: What's on Today counts today. Nothing else.
captions: Before: The Backlog collects everything that is coming up at some point. Today is empty.
Morning: You pull two tasks over to Today, the rest stays where it is.
During the day: You tick one task off and it moves down to the completed ones.
3 AM: The day ends. What you finished moves to the Archive under Completed, what you didn't under Archived.
Next morning: Today is empty again. You decide anew.

blocks.heading: Sorted by time horizon, not by priority
blocks.lead: Priorities are a lie you tell yourself. In the end everything is important. So Dawny asks something simpler: roughly when?
list: Quick for everything that takes a few minutes
Next couple of days for what is due this week
Next couple of weeks and Next couple of months for the rest
your own categories, as many as you like, each with its own symbol
recurring categories as a special case
blocks.close: Each morning you pull what you trust yourself to do from any of these groups over to Today. The rest stays visible without getting in the way.
blocks.imageAlt: The Backlog in Dawny with the categories sorted by time horizon

blocks.heading: Today is deliberately short
blocks.lead: Two sections, nothing else: Open and Completed. No projects, no tags, no subtasks, no colours telling you how bad you should feel.
blocks.close: You write a task straight into the line below. One tap ticks it off. To move a task from the Backlog to Today, swipe right.
blocks.imageAlt: The Today view in Dawny with open and completed tasks

blocks.heading: The Archive is not a trash can
blocks.lead: Two things sit side by side in the Archive: under Completed, everything you managed, sorted by date. Under Archived, everything that was left undone. None of it is deleted.
blocks.close: Swipe right to bring a task back, either to the Backlog or straight to Today. If you open the app in the morning after the reset, you first get a short overview of what was filed away overnight.
blocks.imageAlt: The Archive in Dawny with the Completed and Archived sections

haltung.heading: A to-do list should not catch you out.
paragraphs: Most lists grow. Whatever you don't manage today is there again tomorrow, and the day after too, just with a red dot next to it. After two weeks the list is a record of everything you missed and you stop opening it.

Dawny turns that around. A spot on the Today list is a commitment for that one day. If you don't keep it, the day is over and the task moves to the Archive, without reproach and without a red dot. It isn't gone, it is just no longer in the way.
Whatever really matters, you bring back. Whatever you don't bring back three times over wasn't it.

widgets.heading: On the home screen, without opening the app
widgets.lead: Three widgets in several sizes: Today, Backlog and Archive. Tasks can be ticked off right in the widget, the app doesn't have to launch for that.
widgets.close: Tapping a line jumps to the matching place in the app. The nightly reset applies to the widgets just the same.
widgets.imageAlt: The Dawny widgets for Today, Backlog and Archive on the iPhone home screen

grid.title: Sync with Reminders
grid.text: If you want, you can mirror the Today list into Apple Reminders. That way your tasks also show up on Mac, iPad and Apple Watch.

grid.title: iCloud sync, optional
grid.text: Turn it on and your iPhone and iPad stay in step, through your own iCloud account, with no outside server.

grid.title: Shortcuts and Siri
grid.text: Create tasks by voice or from an automation, straight into the Backlog or to Today.

grid.title: Three widgets
grid.text: Today, Backlog and Archive, in several sizes. You can tick things off right in the widget, without opening the app.

stats.label: No subscription, no pro version, no in-app purchases.
No registration, no login, no email address.
The app is on GitHub under the MIT license.

vertrauen.note: The app collects nothing. On this website I measure reach anonymously, without cookies. More on that in the privacy policy.

finalCta.heading: Tomorrow morning the list is empty. What will you put on it?
